# `adt wb`

Workbench navigation (where-used, call-hierarchy, definition, outline)

```bash
adt wb [options] [command]
```

**Subcommands**

| Command             | Description                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `adt wb where-used` | Find all usages (where-used) of an ABAP object or symbol                            |
| `adt wb callers`    | Find callers (upward call hierarchy) of a method/function/subroutine                |
| `adt wb callees`    | Find callees (downward call hierarchy) of a method/function/subroutine              |
| `adt wb definition` | Resolve an ABAP symbol (class, interface, function, data element, …) to its ADT URI |
| `adt wb outline`    | Show the structural outline of an ABAP object (includes, methods, attributes, …)    |

## `adt wb where-used`

Find all usages (where-used) of an ABAP object or symbol

```bash
adt wb where-used [options] <object>
```

**Arguments**

| Argument   | Description                          | Default |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `<object>` | Object name to search references for |         |

**Options**

| Option               | Description                             | Default |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `-t, --type <type>`  | Object type (CLAS, PROG, INTF, TABL, …) |         |
| `--uri <uri>`        | Direct ADT URI (skips name resolution)  |         |
| `-m, --max <number>` | Maximum number of results               | `100`   |
| `--json`             | Output results as JSON                  |         |

| `--uri <uri>`        | Direct ADT URI (skips name resolution) |         |
| `-m, --max <number>` | Maximum number of results              | `50`    |
| `--json`             | Output results as JSON                 |         |

## `adt wb definition`

Resolve an ABAP symbol (class, interface, function, data element, …) to its ADT URI

```bash
adt wb definition [options] <reference>
```

**Arguments**

| Argument      | Description                     | Default |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | ------- |
| `<reference>` | Symbol / object name to resolve |         |

**Options**

| Option              | Description                             | Default |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `-t, --type <type>` | Object type (CLAS, PROG, DTEL, TABL, …) |         |
| `--json`            | Output result as JSON                   |         |

## `adt wb outline`

Show the structural outline of an ABAP object (includes, methods, attributes, …)

```bash
adt wb outline [options] <object>
```

**Arguments**

| Argument   | Description | Default |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------- |
| `<object>` | Object name |         |

**Options**

| Option              | Description                                           | Default  |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `-t, --type <type>` | Object type (CLAS, INTF, PROG, FUGR, …)               |          |
| `--version <v>`     | Object version to inspect: active \| inactive         | `active` |
| `--json`            | Output as JSON (default pretty-prints JSON structure) |          |

Global options (`--sid`, `--config`, `--verbose`, …) are accepted by every command — see the [command reference index](./index.md#global-options).
